title: The Unreliable Voice
text:
Scholars of the modern novel frequently return to the question of who is really speaking when a story unfolds. A narrator who seems authoritative may be concealing bias, selective memory, or an unacknowledged desire to persuade. Such narrators reward the attentive reader, who learns to read between the lines of confident assertions.

Consider how a reader's trust is gradually eroded by small inconsistencies: a date that does not add up, a description that contradicts an earlier one. Critics argue that this erosion is not a flaw but a deliberate invitation to reconstruct the events independently. The novel thus becomes a puzzle in which the reader must assemble the truth from fragments the narrator has carelessly scattered.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what may a seemingly authoritative narrator be concealing?
options: Bias, selective memory, or a desire to persuade
The exact date on which the story takes place
Information about the author's personal life
Evidence that the events never happened

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do small inconsistencies do to the reader's trust?
options: They have no effect on it
They cause the reader to stop reading

questions.text: What does the author suggest about the reader of an unreliable narrator?
options: The reader must actively reconstruct the truth rather than accept the narrator's account
The reader should trust the narrator's confident assertions
The reader is usually misled and cannot recover the events
The reader benefits most from avoiding the text's inconsistencies

questions.text: Why do critics regard the erosion of trust as deliberate rather than a flaw?
options: Because it shows that the author made careless mistakes
Because it allows the narrator to avoid all responsibility
Because it invites the reader to reconstruct events independently
Because it makes the novel shorter and easier to read

vocabulary.definition: to cause someone to believe or do something through reasons or argument
differences between statements or details that do not agree with each other
the gradual wearing away of something over time

paragraph_translations: Modern romanın araştırmacıları, bir hikâye açıldığında gerçekte kimin konuştuğu sorusuna sık sık dönerler. Otoriter görünen bir anlatıcı, önyargıyı, seçici hafızayı ya da kabul edilmemiş bir ikna isteğini gizlemiş olabilir. Bu tür anlatıcılar, özgüvenli iddiaların satır aralarını okumayı öğrenen dikkatli okuru ödüllendirir.

Küçük tutarsızlıkların okurun güvenini nasıl yavaş yavaş aşındırdığını düşünün: toplamayan bir tarih, daha önce verilen bir betimlemeyle çelişen başka bir betimleme. Eleştirmenler bu aşınmanın bir kusur değil, olayları bağımsız olarak yeniden kurma yönünde bilerek yapılmış bir davet olduğunu savunur. Roman böylece, okurun anlatıcının özensizce saçtığı parçalardan gerçeği bir araya getirmesi gereken bir bulmacaya dönüşür.
